commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Replace AB3 requirements with ClubLogistics scope
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide requirements still describe AB3 contact management.

They need to reflect the team's ClubLogistics direction and preserve all
identified requirements for future reference.

Let's replace the target user profile and value proposition, and document
the prioritized user stories, representative use cases, non-functional
requirements, and glossary.

Include both MVP and deferred requirements so the Developer Guide describes

commitResults.messageTitle: README: Replace sample project text with ClubLogistics overview
commitResults.messageBody:
The README still presents the repository as the sample AddressBook project.

This does not explain ClubLogistics, its target user, or its equipment
tracking purpose to project visitors.

Let's replace the sample text with a product overview, key capabilities,
and links to the project documentation.

Focus the content on the intended product so readers can understand the
project without referring to the original AddressBook materials.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add project guidance for AI agents
commitResults.messageBody:
AI agents currently lack shared instructions for working on this project.

Without project-specific guidance, agents may use the wrong Java version,
overlook important tests, or follow inconsistent Git practices.

Let's document the Java 25 requirement, testing expectations, and Git
conventions in AGENTS.md for all agents to follow.

Keep the instructions in one place and let CLAUDE.md reference them so
different AI tools apply the same project standards.

Equipment can be added to the register, but a record that was entered
by mistake or is no longer tracked cannot be removed. The register can
only grow, so incorrect records stay in it permanently.

The MVP needs a remove command so the coordinator can correct the
register, and the work is split across several PRs so it can be
extended next week.

Let's add a remove <equipment-id> command that deletes an existing
item, matching the ID without regard to case. The model gains
findEquipment and removeEquipment, backed by find and remove in
UniqueEquipmentList. The command rejects unknown IDs and bad formats
with the messages from the MVP specification.

This is a partial implementation. Rejecting the removal of issued
equipment is not included because the borrower field from the issue
command is not on master yet. A TODO in RemoveCommand marks the spot.
The UserGuide section is also left for a later PR.

Jared's Role and Responsibilities lines are written as plain lines,

commitResults.messageTitle: Return command: Add parser for return equipment
commitResults.messageBody:
The app can add, list and remove equipment, but it has no way to
record that issued equipment has been returned.

Returning equipment depends on the issue command's borrower field,
which is not yet on master. Parsing the command input does not depend
on it, so it can be built and reviewed separately now.

Let's add ReturnCommandParser, which accepts exactly one equipment ID
and validates it with the same EquipmentId rules used by add and
remove. Let's also register the return command word in
AddressBookParser and add a placeholder ReturnCommand whose execute
reports that the command is not yet supported without touching the
model.

Reusing EquipmentId keeps ID validation and case-insensitive matching
consistent across commands, as the feature spec requires. The parser
mirrors RemoveCommandParser so that both single-ID commands behave the
same way on missing or extra arguments.

The errors for equipment that does not exist or is not currently
issued depend on the model and will be added with the return logic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

AddressBookParserTest imports RemoveCommand, but no test in the file
uses it after master was merged into this branch. The issue equipment
change on master removed the remove command parser tests, while the
import stayed because this branch also edits the neighbouring import
lines.

Checkstyle rejects unused imports, so the CI build for this branch
fails.

Let's remove the unused RemoveCommand import.

Removing the import is the smallest change that fixes the build. It
does not reintroduce the remove parser tests that master deliberately
dropped.
